consumed_owner_ratifications.statement_verbatim: The recommended Evaluate result is deterministic SYSTEM output derived from the deterministic Score plus an immutable/versioned DecisionPolicy. Stella may provide rationale/analysis only and may not choose the authoritative recommendation.
When the denominator is zero or all applicable items are N/A, the Evaluate result is SCORE_NOT_COMPUTABLE. This is a fail-closed transition reason and blocks a decision.
DecisionPolicy bands must be ordered, non-overlapping and exhaustive inside the immutable policy version.
Decision outcomes are exactly: approve, approve_with_conditions, reject. No other outcome value is authorized.

Default decision role is organization_admin. Allowed designated decision roles are organization_admin and impact_manager. super_admin, analyst, reviewer, and viewer are forbidden as decision roles. No '+' hierarchy notation may implicitly admit super_admin.
Divergence is derived from the snapshotted recommended_outcome versus the decision_outcome. A rationale is mandatory when they diverge.
Stella Evaluate analysis reuses the existing 'advisor' capability with pipeline_step='evaluate_analysis'. No new G2 category is created by this decision.

Terminal Evaluate lifecycle state is ARCHIVED. Archiving is allowed only before DECIDED and requires impact_manager or the specific separately-authorized role semantics that do NOT admit platform super_admin by hierarchy.
impact_manager may draft an Evaluate template. Publishing or retiring a template requires organization_admin.
Evaluate routes are: project evaluations, and organization templates. No new first-level navigation item is required solely by this authority.

Platform superadmin bypass is prohibited for all Evaluate tenant content. Platform support may access Evaluate content only through a separately authorized bounded support capability under the operator model.
Evaluate is included in Commercial V1. The future capability key evaluate.v1 is reserved. The key itself is not authority to implement a new entitlement system.
Evaluate V1 uses the in-app read model only. No Evaluate PDF/report/public-verification artifact, and no table named evaluation_results, is authorized by this decision.

Evaluate V1 does NOT use first-class stella_findings and does NOT require an approved SROI run. Therefore broad Evaluate does not depend on Wave3. A narrow run-review FIB surface may retain its independent Wave3 dependency.
PR106 is superseded. The successor Evaluate authority must be a fresh authority lane from current live, not an amendment performed inside PR106.

Evaluate criterion responses may be created or edited before their governing lock only by the exact explicit role set {analyst, impact_manager, organization_admin}. reviewer does not edit criterion responses. viewer is read-only. super_admin is excluded from this edit set. No '+' hierarchy notation and no implicit higher-role admission apply.

consumed_owner_ratifications.statement_verbatim: Commercial V1 does not require person-inequality between the criterion-input author, the reviewer, and the decision maker. binding_semantics_verbatim.org_level_stricter_policy_permitted: An organization may layer a stricter separation-of-duties policy on top of this floor; this ratification does not forbid that, it only refuses to mandate it at the Commercial V1 platform level.
binding_semantics_verbatim.unchanged_rules: Existing decision-role assignment, divergence handling, and mandatory-rationale-on-divergence rules are not altered by this ratification.

explicit_non_authorizations_verbatim: Does not authorize an organization-configurable segregation-of-duties feature; it only permits one to exist as future scope.
Does not alter existing divergence/mandatory-rationale mechanics.

STATE_MACHINE.hd08_terminal_note: HD-08 states 'Terminal Evaluate lifecycle state is ARCHIVED'. This authority reads that as ARCHIVED being terminal — which it is — and not as a claim that DECIDED is non-terminal: HD-08's own next sentence ('Archiving is allowed only before DECIDED') presupposes that a DECIDED evaluation can no longer be archived, which is only coherent if DECIDED is itself terminal. Both are terminal; they are the two absorbing states of the machine.
STATE_MACHINE.score_status_is_not_a_state: SCORE_NOT_COMPUTABLE is deliberately NOT a state. HD-02 calls it 'a fail-closed transition REASON', which is precisely a guard and not a state. It is a DERIVED property of the current criterion responses against the pinned template version, recomputed on every read. Making it a state would let a stored value go stale relative to the responses that determine it, and a stale 'COMPUTED' would unblock a decision that must be blocked.
STATE_MACHINE.archived_is_terminal_and_pre_decision_on: There is NO transition out of ARCHIVED and NO transition from DECIDED to ARCHIVED (HD-08). An organization that wants to withdraw a decided evaluation records that as a NEW evaluation, because a decided evaluation is audit-bearing evidence that a human decided.

GOVERNING_LOCK.definition: The governing lock for criterion responses is the transition into DECIDED (T5).
GOVERNING_LOCK.why_this_authority_decides_it: RAT-EV-02 constrains WHO may create or edit criterion responses 'before their governing lock' and its explicit_non_authorizations state that it 'does not decide lock timing/state-machine mechanics beyond before the governing lock'. Fixing the lock is therefore this authority's job, not an open gap.
GOVERNING_LOCK.why_DECIDED: HD-06 derives divergence from the SNAPSHOTTED recommended_outcome. A snapshot is only meaningful if the inputs that produced it can no longer change. If criterion responses stayed editable after DECIDED, the Score would drift away from score_snapshot and the divergence record would describe a computation nobody could reproduce. DECIDED is therefore the only transition at which the lock can fall without breaking HD-06.
GOVERNING_LOCK.archived_interaction: ARCHIVED is pre-decision and terminal, so no criterion response may be created or edited on an ARCHIVED evaluation either — not because the lock fell, but because the evaluation is withdrawn. Both refusals are required; they have different reasons and are tested separately.

TRANSITION_MATRIX.enforcement_layers: Enforced in the SERVER ACTION (authoritative) and, where a transition is also expressible as a database constraint, additionally at the database as defense in depth. A UI that hides a button is NOT an enforcement layer.

SCORING.determinism: The Score is a PURE function of (the pinned template version's criteria_json, the current projection of OBJ-4 responses). It reads no clock, no random source, no environment variable and no AI output. The same inputs always yield the same Score (HD-01).
SCORING.governed_na_arithmetic: Per EV-01, a criterion whose current response_kind = 'NOT_APPLICABLE' is excluded from the numerator AND the denominator. It is not scored as zero and it is not scored as the maximum.
SCORING.readiness_is_a_different_domain: EV-01 explicitly permits Measure readiness to use a different governed-N/A arithmetic. This package binds ONLY Evaluate scoring. It does NOT change, reinterpret or align lib/pipeline readiness arithmetic, and an implementer must not refactor the two into a shared helper on the assumption that they agree.

score_status.COMPUTED: The denominator is greater than zero — at least one criterion has a current SCORED response.
score_status.SCORE_NOT_COMPUTABLE: HD-02's two conditions: the denominator is zero, OR all applicable items are N/A. Under EV-01's exclusion rule the second reduces to the first, which is why one status value covers both and why there is no second code path.
score_status.hd02_classification: HD-02 calls this 'a fail-closed transition reason' that 'blocks a decision'. It is therefore a guard on T5, not a state and not an error to be recovered from.
score_status.derivation: score_status is computed, never stored outside the DECIDED snapshot.

SCORING.unanswered_is_not_na: An UNANSWERED criterion (no OBJ-4 row at all for that criterion_key) is NOT a governed N/A. It blocks T3 rather than being excluded from the denominator. Conflating the two would let an empty evaluation reach READY_FOR_DECISION with a vacuous SCORE_NOT_COMPUTABLE and would make HD-02's block indistinguishable from ordinary incompleteness.

ZERO_DENOMINATOR_CONTROLS.control: SCORE_NOT_COMPUTABLE is the NAME of the zero-denominator condition, not a separate error path.
ZERO_DENOMINATOR_CONTROLS.rationale: EV-01's rule — N/A excluded from numerator AND denominator — makes an all-N/A evaluation arithmetically scoreless BY CONSTRUCTION, and HD-02 names both conditions as producing the one status. An implementation with a separate divide-by-zero guard and a separate SCORE_NOT_COMPUTABLE flag has two things that can disagree.

ZERO_DENOMINATOR_CONTROLS.control: The scoring function NEVER performs a division whose denominator it has not first proven greater than zero. It returns a discriminated result carrying score_status, not a number plus a nullable error.

No NaN, no Infinity, no null-coerced-to-zero and no sentinel numeric value (such as -1 or 0) may ever represent SCORE_NOT_COMPUTABLE. A sentinel number would be comparable against DecisionPolicy bands and could silently produce a recommended outcome.

The SYSTEM recommended outcome is NOT produced when score_status = 'SCORE_NOT_COMPUTABLE'. It is absent, not defaulted to 'reject' and not defaulted to 'approve_with_conditions'. A default would be the system deciding, which HD-01 reserves to the deterministic Score-plus-policy derivation and EV-02 reserves the decision itself to the human.
T5 REFUSES when score_status computed at decision time is 'SCORE_NOT_COMPUTABLE' (HD-02). The refusal is server-authoritative and audited as a refusal, never a silent no-op.

A template version whose criteria_json contains ZERO criteria may not be published. An empty criteria set makes every evaluation against it permanently SCORE_NOT_COMPUTABLE, which is a template defect, not a governed outcome.

DECISION_OUTCOMES.anchor: HD-04: 'Decision outcomes are exactly: approve, approve_with_conditions, reject. No other outcome value is authorized.'
DECISION_OUTCOMES.note: Enforced as a CLOSED CHECK constraint on OBJ-3.decision_outcome AND on OBJ-3.recommended_outcome_snapshot, and as a closed union in the type layer. No 'pending', no 'deferred', no 'abstain', no null-as-outcome. An evaluation with no outcome is expressed by its STATE, not by a fourth outcome value.
DECISION_OUTCOMES.shared_domain_is_deliberate: recommended_outcome_snapshot and decision_outcome draw from the SAME closed set of three. That is what makes divergence computable as a simple inequality (HD-06, DIV-02). If the SYSTEM recommendation had its own vocabulary, divergence would require a mapping table and the mapping would become a place to hide a disagreement.

DECISION_POLICY.definition: The DecisionPolicy is the deterministic function that maps a COMPUTED Score to exactly one member of DECISION_OUTCOMES. It is data, stored as decision_policy_json inside the immutable OBJ-2 row (EV-02, HD-01).

band_requirements.anchor: HD-03: 'DecisionPolicy bands must be ordered, non-overlapping and exhaustive inside the immutable policy version.'
band_requirements.ordered: The bands are stored and evaluated in a defined monotonic order over the score domain. Order is a PUBLICATION-TIME property of the stored policy, not an incidental property of however the evaluator happens to iterate — an evaluator that produces the right answer from unordered bands still fails HD-03, because the stored policy is what the ratification constrains.
band_requirements.non_overlapping: No score value falls in two bands.
band_requirements.exhaustive: Every representable COMPUTED score value falls in exactly one band. Together with non-overlapping this is totality.
band_requirements.no_fallback_branch: A policy needing a fallback is not exhaustive and must be REJECTED AT PUBLICATION, not patched at evaluation time. A fallback branch is how a non-exhaustive policy passes for an exhaustive one.
band_requirements.boundary_closure: Band boundaries are explicit and closed on a stated side. A policy that leaves a boundary value ambiguous is not publishable — ambiguity at a boundary is an overlap or a gap, and HD-03 forbids both.
band_requirements.reads_only_the_score: The policy reads ONLY the Score. It does not read the actor, the project, the clock, the organization's plan, or any Stella output.

version_identity.identity_is: The DecisionPolicy version identity IS the template version identity. There is no second, independent policy version lineage.
components: definition_hash (over the whole immutable version payload)
version_identity.why_two_hashes: definition_hash proves the whole version is unchanged. decision_policy_hash proves specifically WHICH policy produced a recommended outcome, so a snapshotted recommendation stays attributable. OBJ-3 snapshots decision_policy_hash_snapshot, not the policy body.
version_identity.pattern_source: governed_model_registry's (model_id, version) UNIQUE plus definition_hash, adopted as a PATTERN and re-hosted inside an organization-scoped relation (DRR-02).
version_identity.immutability_enforcement: UPDATE and DELETE denied by RLS policy OMISSION on OBJ-2 except for the single write-once publication transition (OBJ-2.publication_write_once), plus the uellix_forbid_mutation trigger constrained to the same exception — the 0045 precedent, including its stated position that the trigger is 'defense in depth, not the only guard'.

DECISION_POLICY.pinning: An evaluation pins template_version_id at creation (T1) and that pin is NEVER repointed. Publishing a new template version, or retiring the container, has ZERO effect on any existing evaluation, decided or not. A recommended outcome is therefore always reproducible from the version that produced it.

SYSTEM_RECOMMENDATION.producer: The SYSTEM, deterministically, from (Score, pinned immutable DecisionPolicy). Never Stella, never a human, never a default (HD-01).
SYSTEM_RECOMMENDATION.hd01_verbatim_anchor: 'The recommended Evaluate result is deterministic SYSTEM output derived from the deterministic Score plus an immutable/versioned DecisionPolicy. Stella may provide rationale/analysis only and may not choose the authoritative recommendation.'
SYSTEM_RECOMMENDATION.visibility: Displayed in the in-app read model whenever score_status = 'COMPUTED', from READY_FOR_DECISION onward. It is ADVICE TO THE HUMAN, and it never auto-applies.
SYSTEM_RECOMMENDATION.snapshot: At T5, recommended_outcome_snapshot is written in the SAME statement as decision_outcome. It records what the system recommended AT THE MOMENT OF DECISION.
SYSTEM_RECOMMENDATION.why_snapshot_rather_than_recompute: HD-06 requires divergence to be derived from the SNAPSHOTTED recommended_outcome. Recomputing it later would make a historical divergence finding change after the fact. A snapshot makes the divergence record permanent.
SYSTEM_RECOMMENDATION.no_auto_decision: There is no path, flag, cron, batch job or admin action by which the SYSTEM recommended outcome becomes the decision without a designated human performing T5. EV-02's 'Human decision remains decisive' is enforced by the absence of any such path, and NSB-05 is the control that proves the absence.

DIVERGENCE_CONTROLS.control: Divergence exists only for a DECIDED evaluation. A pre-DECIDED evaluation has no decision_outcome, so it has no divergence VALUE at all — which is different from having a divergence of 'false'.

Divergence is DERIVED as (recommended_outcome_snapshot IS NOT NULL AND decision_outcome != recommended_outcome_snapshot). It is computed from the two snapshot columns on read. It is NOT stored (HD-06).
DIVERGENCE_CONTROLS.rationale: A stored divergence flag is a third value that can disagree with the two it summarizes. Deriving it makes disagreement impossible by construction.

DIVERGENCE_CONTROLS.control: decision_rationale is MANDATORY when decision_outcome != recommended_outcome_snapshot, enforced server-side at T5 AND as a database CHECK constraint over the row (a decided row where the two outcomes differ and decision_rationale is NULL or empty must be unrepresentable, not merely unreachable through the action).
DIVERGENCE_CONTROLS.rationale: HD-06. Enforcing this only in the action leaves the invariant true by convention rather than by construction.

DIVERGENCE_CONTROLS.control: decision_rationale is PERMITTED but not required when decision_outcome == recommended_outcome_snapshot. Agreement needs no justification; disagreement does.

A decided evaluation whose score_status_snapshot is 'SCORE_NOT_COMPUTABLE' cannot exist, because T5 refuses that case (ZD-05). Therefore recommended_outcome_snapshot is NEVER NULL on a DECIDED row, and divergence is always well-defined for a decided evaluation. Stated explicitly so no implementer adds a 'divergence unknown' third value to cover a case the state machine already forecloses.

Divergence is auditable WITHOUT reading rationale text: the audit event evaluation.decision_recorded carries the two outcome VALUES (both members of a closed three-value enum, and therefore not tenant content) plus a hash of the rationale. The rationale TEXT stays in OBJ-3 behind bypass-free RLS. See NSB-04.

RAT-EV-03 does not alter any of DIV-01..DIV-06. Its own binding_semantics say so ('Existing decision-role assignment, divergence handling, and mandatory-rationale-on-divergence rules are not altered by this ratification'). Stated explicitly because closing a separation-of-duties gap is the kind of change under which a divergence rule could be quietly relaxed.

EVALUATE_DECISION_ROLES.semantics: SET INCLUSION over an exhaustively enumerated two-element set, checked by exact identity.
EVALUATE_DECISION_ROLES.role_space_partition: 2 + 4 = 6, equal to the six values in the db/schema.ts role CHECK.
EVALUATE_DECISION_ROLES.uniformity_note: R4 mirrors the exclusion list onto this set so all SEVEN closed sets carry the same shape (members + excluded + partition). R2/R3 kept the decision exclusions only in the sibling key forbidden_decision_roles, which is preserved unchanged for existing citations - but a validator iterating the seven sets uniformly could not read them, and a set whose exclusions live somewhere else is a set whose partition cannot be checked the same way as its peers.

EVALUATE_CRITERION_EDIT_ROLES.semantics: SET INCLUSION over an exhaustively enumerated three-element set. RAT-EV-02's binding_semantics require that 'each admitted role must be checked by exact identity, not by rank'.
EVALUATE_CRITERION_EDIT_ROLES.role_space_partition: 3 admitted + 3 excluded = 6, equal to the six values in the db/schema.ts role CHECK. No role is unaccounted for.
EVALUATE_CRITERION_EDIT_ROLES.distinct_from_decision_set: This set is NOT the decision set and must never be conflated with it. analyst may EDIT a criterion response and may NEVER decide. organization_admin and impact_manager appear in BOTH sets, which is exactly why a single shared helper would be a defect: it would silently admit analyst to the decision path or strip analyst from the edit path depending on which set it collapsed to. Two separate closed sets, two separate predicates.
EVALUATE_CRITERION_EDIT_ROLES.reviewer_is_the_trap: reviewer is EXCLUDED from criterion editing (RAT-EV-02) and EXCLUDED from deciding (HD-05), yet reviewer IS a member of the repository's existing REVIEW_ROLES/isInReviewSet. An implementer reaching for isInReviewSet because Evaluate 'feels like review tooling' would admit reviewer to both Evaluate sets in one move. Neither Evaluate set may be derived from isInReviewSet.

ROLE_MATRIX.default_designated_decision_role: organization_admin (HD-05). Applied as the column default AND as the explicit value written at T1 when the caller supplies none — never left to a nullable column interpreted as 'the default'.
ROLE_MATRIX.designation_rule: Only organization_admin or impact_manager may be designated as an evaluation's decider (HD-05). Any other value is REFUSED at T1 and is unrepresentable in the column (CLOSED CHECK).

forbidden_decision_roles.note: super_admin is forbidden not because it is insufficiently privileged but because platform administration is not tenant decision-making (HD-12, MO-07). 2 admitted + 4 forbidden = 6, partitioning the schema role CHECK exactly.

enforcement_mechanism.required: Closed set-inclusion predicates, declared once in lib/auth/permissions.ts alongside the EXISTING STELLA_ROLES and REVIEW_ROLES precedents: const EVALUATE_DECISION_ROLES: readonly Role[] = ['organization_admin','impact_manager'] and const EVALUATE_CRITERION_EDIT_ROLES: readonly Role[] = ['analyst','impact_manager','organization_admin'], each consumed by its own .includes(role) predicate.
enforcement_mechanism.FORBIDDEN: hasRole() is forbidden for EVERY Evaluate predicate — decision, criterion edit, archive, template draft and template publish/retire alike. No '+', no >=, no 'and above', no implicit higher-role admission (HD-05, RAT-EV-02).
enforcement_mechanism.measured_reason: hasRole is ROLE_HIERARCHY[userRole] >= ROLE_HIERARCHY[requiredRole]. Measured: super_admin = 100 dominates every other role, so hasRole('super_admin', X) is TRUE for every X. Concretely hasRole(role,'analyst') — the shape an implementer would naturally reach for to express the criterion-edit set, since analyst is its lowest-ranked member — admits analyst, impact_manager, organization_admin AND super_admin, and ALSO happens to exclude reviewer and viewer correctly. It therefore produces the right answer for five of six roles and the WRONG answer for exactly the one role RAT-EV-02 names as excluded. That near-correctness is what makes it dangerous: a test suite checking that reviewer and viewer are denied passes.
enforcement_mechanism.not_a_new_mechanism: lib/auth/permissions.ts already carries two set-inclusion sets for exactly this reason and says so in its own comments. This package selects the existing pattern rather than introducing one.
enforcement_mechanism.guard_non_collision: lib/auth/__tests__/no-inline-review-role-arrays.test.ts targets only lib/pipeline/sroi-results.ts and lib/pipeline/methodology-review.ts and matches only arrays containing 'reviewer'. Both Evaluate sets live in lib/auth/permissions.ts and neither contains 'reviewer'. No collision.
enforcement_mechanism.runtime_role_source: The acting role must come from the actor's membership in THE EVALUATION'S organization, resolved server-side (current_user_role_in_org(org_id) at the database layer, the session helper at the application layer). It must NEVER come from a client-supplied field, an ambient 'current role' resolved against a different organization, or a platform-level flag.

permission_matrix.grant: NOT SEPARATELY OWNER-RATIFIED. Classified BOUNDED_IMPLEMENTATION_CHOICE; see CREATE_AUTHORITY_DISCLOSURE and RESIDUAL_NOTES.RN-04. R4 gives this its OWN constant - R3 read EVALUATE_DECISION_ROLES, which was CA-B-01.

permission_matrix.mechanism: EXACT_SET_INCLUSION over EVALUATE_CRITERION_EDIT_ROLES, PLUS the evaluation being pre-lock
EXACT_SET_INCLUSION over EVALUATE_DECISION_ROLES, PLUS equality against the evaluation's designated_decision_role
permission_matrix.grant: HD-05. Both conditions: set membership alone would let an impact_manager decide an evaluation designated to organization_admin.

HD-08. impact_manager is named in HD-08; organization_admin is admitted under HD-08's 'specific separately-authorized role semantics that do NOT admit platform super_admin by hierarchy', exercised here as an exact two-element enumeration. R4 gives this its OWN constant - R3 read EVALUATE_DECISION_ROLES, which was CA-B-01.
RAT-EV-04. Closes BR B-01. Extensionally equal to EVALUATE_DECISION_ROLES today and STILL A DISTINCT PREDICATE - see PREDICATE_IDENTITY_SEPARATION.
RAT-EV-04, restating HD-09. impact_manager is excluded: draft authority does not extend to publish.
RAT-EV-04, restating HD-09. Extensionally equal to the publish set today and STILL A DISTINCT PREDICATE.

Read access is tenancy-scoped, not role-gated beyond membership. viewer is read-only per RAT-EV-02 and reviewer may read though it may not edit. super_admin is NOT admitted by any Evaluate-specific bypass (HD-12, NSB-02).

EVALUATE_TEMPLATE_DRAFT_ROLES.semantics: SET INCLUSION by EXACT ROLE IDENTITY over an exhaustively enumerated two-element set. Never by rank, threshold or '+' notation.
EVALUATE_TEMPLATE_DRAFT_ROLES.role_space_partition: 2 admitted + 4 excluded = 6, equal to the six values in the db/schema.ts role CHECK.
EVALUATE_TEMPLATE_DRAFT_ROLES.R2_CORRECTION: R2 expressed this as the one-element set {impact_manager}, reading HD-09's 'impact_manager may draft' as 'only impact_manager may draft'. RAT-EV-04 ratifies that organization_admin may ALSO draft. This is BR blocker B-01, closed.

EVALUATE_TEMPLATE_PUBLISH_ROLES.semantics: SET INCLUSION by EXACT ROLE IDENTITY over a one-element set.
EVALUATE_TEMPLATE_PUBLISH_ROLES.impact_manager_explicitly_excluded: RAT-EV-04: 'impact_manager's draft authority does not extend to publish or retire.' A role in the draft set is NOT thereby in the publish set.

EVALUATE_TEMPLATE_RETIRE_ROLES.semantics: SET INCLUSION by EXACT ROLE IDENTITY over a one-element set.
EVALUATE_TEMPLATE_RETIRE_ROLES.distinct_from_publish_despite_equal_exte: Retire and publish have IDENTICAL extensions today. They remain two authority concepts with two predicates. See PREDICATE_IDENTITY_SEPARATION.

EVALUATE_ARCHIVE_ROLES.anchor: HD-08, verbatim: 'Terminal Evaluate lifecycle state is ARCHIVED. Archiving is allowed only before DECIDED and requires impact_manager or the specific separately-authorized role semantics that do NOT admit platform super_admin by hierarchy.'
EVALUATE_ARCHIVE_ROLES.canonical_derivation: impact_manager is admitted BY NAME in HD-08. organization_admin is admitted because HD-08 expressly permits 'the specific separately-authorized role semantics that do NOT admit platform super_admin by hierarchy', and this authority exercises that clause with an EXACT two-element enumeration that admits super_admin neither by hierarchy nor by enumeration. The constant is therefore HD-08-anchored in both of its members.
EVALUATE_ARCHIVE_ROLES.semantics: SET INCLUSION by EXACT ROLE IDENTITY over an exhaustively enumerated two-element set.
EVALUATE_ARCHIVE_ROLES.role_space_partition: 2 + 4 = 6, equal to the six values in the db/schema.ts role CHECK.
EVALUATE_ARCHIVE_ROLES.R3_DEFECT_CLOSED: R3 bound canArchiveEvaluation to EVALUATE_DECISION_ROLES and annotated it 'consumed, not redefined'. That annotation described a violation of R3's own rule rather than curing it. canArchiveEvaluation now reads THIS constant and only this constant. The extension is unchanged; only its identity is now its own.
EVALUATE_ARCHIVE_ROLES.extensional_equality_is_irrelevant: This set is extensionally equal to EVALUATE_DECISION_ROLES and to EVALUATE_TEMPLATE_DRAFT_ROLES today. That is a coincidence of current membership, not an identity. A future amendment to HD-05 or RAT-EV-04 must not move this set, and a future amendment to HD-08 must not move theirs.

EVALUATE_CREATE_ROLES.canonical_status: NO canonical ratification addresses who may CREATE an Evaluate evaluation. Measured for this revision: a case-insensitive search for 'creat* an evaluation', 'evaluation creation', 'canCreateEvaluation' and 'who may create' across all three canonical ledgers (EVALUATE_OWNER_RATIFICATIONS_v1.0.0.json, COMMERCIAL_V1_MICRO_RATIFICATIONS_v1.0.0.json, COMMERCIAL_V1_MICRO_RATIFICATIONS_AMENDMENT_v1.0.1.json) returns ZERO hits in each.
EVALUATE_CREATE_ROLES.semantics: SET INCLUSION by EXACT ROLE IDENTITY over an exhaustively enumerated two-element set.
EVALUATE_CREATE_ROLES.current_chosen_extension_rationale: Creating an evaluation binds a project to a pinned immutable template version. This authority keeps that act at the same membership as the governance acts rather than widening it, because widening would be the only unsafe direction available without a ratification. The extension is UNCHANGED from R3; R4 changes its IDENTITY, not its membership.
EVALUATE_CREATE_ROLES.R3_DEFECT_CLOSED: R3's permission_matrix bound canCreateEvaluation to EVALUATE_DECISION_ROLES. It now reads THIS constant and only this constant, so a future amendment to HD-05 cannot silently move the create set.
EVALUATE_CREATE_ROLES.future_authority: Widening or otherwise changing this extension beyond the current bounded choice requires future owner ratification and, where applicable, the corresponding review. Narrowing it is likewise a future decision, not an implementation liberty. See CREATE_AUTHORITY_DISCLOSURE and RESIDUAL_NOTES.RN-04.

SEPARATION_OF_DUTIES.disposition: NO PERSON-INEQUALITY IS REQUIRED IN COMMERCIAL V1.
SEPARATION_OF_DUTIES.anchor: RAT-EV-03: 'Commercial V1 does not require person-inequality between the criterion-input author, the reviewer, and the decision maker.'
SEPARATION_OF_DUTIES.what_this_means_concretely: The same natural person may record a criterion response, submit the evaluation for decision, and record the decision — provided that person holds a role in each required set for each act. A single organization_admin can perform the whole journey, because organization_admin is in both EVALUATE_CRITERION_EDIT_ROLES and EVALUATE_DECISION_ROLES. An analyst cannot, because analyst is in neither the decision set nor the archive set.
SEPARATION_OF_DUTIES.what_is_NOT_relaxed: Role restrictions are untouched. RAT-EV-03 relaxes PERSON inequality, never ROLE membership. The same person still needs the right ROLE for each act, and no act becomes reachable by a role that HD-05 or RAT-EV-02 excludes.
SEPARATION_OF_DUTIES.run_review_precedent_not_imported: The repository's existing SoD rule — canApproveRunMethodology = isInReviewSet(role) && !isRunAuthor, enforced by assertRunMethodologyApprovalAllowed — is NOT imported into Evaluate (DRR-06). It governs the narrow FIB run-review surface and stays there. Importing it would impose at the platform level what the owner explicitly refused to mandate.
SEPARATION_OF_DUTIES.org_level_stricter_policy: An organization MAY layer a stricter separation-of-duties policy on top of the traceability floor. This authority does not forbid that and does not build it: RAT-EV-03's own explicit_non_authorizations state it 'does not authorize an organization-configurable segregation-of-duties feature; it only permits one to exist as future scope'. No configuration surface, setting, column or toggle for it is authorized here.

TRACEABILITY_FLOOR.anchor: RAT-EV-03 binding_semantics.traceability_floor: 'Actor identity, role at time of action, response/version, and timestamp must be preserved for every criterion-input, review, and decision action, regardless of whether the same or different people performed them.'
four_required_facts_per_action: ACTOR — the user id, server-resolved, never client-supplied
ROLE AT TIME OF ACTION — snapshotted, because a user's role in an organization can change after the act
VERSION — which response/version the action produced or acted on
TRACEABILITY_FLOOR.why_this_forced_a_model_correction: R1 modelled criterion responses as an overwriting upsert keyed UNIQUE (evaluation_id, criterion_key). An overwrite destroys the actor, role and timestamp of the response it replaces, so the floor's 'for every criterion-input action' could not be met and an organization could not distinguish the author of a response from its later editor — the very distinction a stricter SoD policy needs. OBJ-4 is therefore append-only with an ordinal (OBJ-4.R2_CORRECTION).
TRACEABILITY_FLOOR.review_action_note: RAT-EV-03's floor names a 'review' action, but no HD ratification defines a distinct Evaluate review state or action, and RAT-EV-02 removes reviewer from criterion editing. This package therefore does NOT invent a review action in order to have something to trace. The floor is satisfied for every action that EXISTS, and any future ratified Evaluate review action inherits the same four facts without amendment to this section. Recorded as RESIDUAL_NOTES.RN-02 rather than silently dropped.
TRACEABILITY_FLOOR.role_at_action_is_not_derivable_later: Every role_at_action column is REQUIRED and may never be reconstructed by joining to current membership at read time. A user whose role changed after the act would then be reported with the wrong role, which would silently falsify exactly the record an organization would rely on to audit its own stricter policy.

TEMPLATE_LIFECYCLE.scope: ORGANIZATION ONLY (HD-10). Every template and every template version belongs to exactly one organization. There is no global, seeded, system or cross-organization template, and no template import/copy path is authorized.

states.meaning: A version being composed. NOT selectable by T1.

states.applies_to: OBJ-2 row with published_at NOT NULL
A PUBLISHED OBJ-2 row that a later version names via supersedes_version_id
states.meaning: DERIVED, not stored as a status. Still fully valid for every evaluation that pinned it. NOT selectable for NEW evaluations.

states.applies_to: OBJ-1 row with retired_at NOT NULL
states.meaning: The container is withdrawn: no new version may be drafted under it, no version may be published under it, and no new evaluation may pin any of its versions. Existing evaluations — including undecided ones — are UNAFFECTED.

role_bindings.anchor: RAT-EV-04 (repository-resident, PR147), which restates HD-09's publish/retire assignment and additively resolves HD-09's draft-set silence.

mutations_covered: create an OBJ-2 row with published_at NULL
compose criteria_json and decision_policy_json on an unpublished OBJ-2 row
the single write-once NULL-to-value transition of published_at / published_by / published_by_role on one OBJ-2 row
set retired_at / retired_by / retired_by_role on one OBJ-1 container

role_bindings.draft_vs_publish_is_a_real_boundary: Draft, publish and retire are THREE different acts on TWO different objects with TWO different role sets, and must be three server actions with three predicates. RAT-EV-04 requires this verbatim: 'a future implementation must express and test all three as distinct checks even though organization_admin satisfies all three.' A single canManageTemplate helper would collapse the whole distinction.
role_bindings.R2_CORRECTION: R2 bound draft to the one-element set {impact_manager} and recorded the operational consequence that an organization whose only privileged member was an organization_admin could not create a template at all. RAT-EV-04 removes that consequence by admitting organization_admin to the draft set. RN-01 is therefore CLOSED, not merely noted.
role_bindings.no_hierarchy: No predicate may be written with hasRole. hasRole(role,'impact_manager') would admit organization_admin AND super_admin to drafting - it would produce the right answer for the draft set's two members and the WRONG answer for super_admin, which RAT-EV-04 excludes by name. hasRole(role,'organization_admin') would admit super_admin to publishing and retiring.

TEMPLATE_LIFECYCLE.publication_is_irreversible: There is no unpublish transition. A published version's criteria and DecisionPolicy are the substrate of every recommended outcome computed from it; retracting it would retroactively unexplain those recommendations. A mistake is corrected by publishing a new version, and the container is withdrawn by RETIRING it — which HD-09 authorizes as its own act — never by editing or unpublishing.
TEMPLATE_LIFECYCLE.immutability_boundary: OBJ-1 metadata (name, description, retirement fields) is mutable. OBJ-2 is append-only in its entirety apart from the single write-once publication transition. Renaming a template does NOT change any version identity, which is why definition_hash covers the VERSION payload and not the container's name.
publication_guards: criteria_json contains at least one criterion (ZD-06)
decision_policy_json bands are ORDERED, non-overlapping and exhaustive with no fallback branch (HD-03)
definition_hash and decision_policy_hash are computed by the server over a canonical serialization, never supplied by the client
version and ordinal are server-assigned and monotonic per template_id
TEMPLATE_LIFECYCLE.retired_container_does_not_orphan_evalua: Retiring OBJ-1 must NOT cascade to OBJ-2 or OBJ-3. A decided evaluation whose template container was later retired remains fully readable and fully explainable. Stated because a CASCADE here would silently destroy decision provenance.
TEMPLATE_LIFECYCLE.AG-01_closed_by: HD-09 (draft/publish/retire split) as additively resolved by RAT-EV-04 (draft set membership).

denial_space_derived.note: The number of template-act refusal cells is DERIVED from the role matrix, not asserted in prose. CA-NB-02 found R3's N-16 prose said 'Twelve' while the control enumerated fourteen cells; a prose count next to a structural list is a second source of truth that can drift.
denial_space_derived.formula: sum over the three template acts of len(excluded) = 4 + 5 + 5 = 14
denial_space_derived.consumed_by: companion manifest N-16, which enumerates exactly this denial space and cites the derived total rather than a hand-written number.

controls.permitted: Stella MAY analyze an evaluation's inputs, explain a criterion, explain the Score, explain the SYSTEM recommended outcome, suggest which criteria look weak, and DRAFT rationale text for a human to review. HD-01 phrases the permission as 'rationale/analysis only'; EV-03 enumerates 'analyze, explain, suggest, draft rationale'.

controls.forbidden: Stella MAY NOT score. No Stella output is an input to the scoring function. The scoring function's signature must make this structurally impossible: it accepts (criteria, responses) and nothing else.

Stella MAY NOT choose the authoritative recommendation (HD-01, verbatim: 'may not choose the authoritative recommendation'). The SYSTEM recommended outcome comes from (Score, DecisionPolicy) only. Any Stella-produced outcome-shaped suggestion is ANALYSIS, is labeled as such in the UI, is never written to recommended_outcome_snapshot, and never participates in the divergence computation.

Stella MAY NOT decide or approve. OBJ-3 carries NO Stella-writable column — no stella_recommendation, no stella_score, no stella_outcome, no stella_analysis. Stella's output lives in stella_interactions.response_json, on the other side of the boundary from the decision record. A STRUCTURAL control, not a review convention: there is no column for Stella to write.

controls.control: Stella Evaluate analysis reuses the EXISTING 'advisor' capability with pipeline_step = 'evaluate_analysis'. No new G2 category is created, and no new stella_role value is added.
controls.measured_consequence: 'advisor' is already one of the six values admitted by stella_interactions_stella_role_check, and pipeline_step is varchar(100) with NO CHECK, so the literal 'evaluate_analysis' is already storable. The Stella Evaluate analysis path therefore requires ZERO DDL. R1 had deferred a Stella binding to DDL_FUTURE; HD-07 retires that requirement.
controls.evaluation_binding: stella_interactions has project_id NOT NULL and NO evaluation_id, so an Evaluate Stella interaction is attributable to the PROJECT and not to a specific evaluation. HD-07 does not require evaluation-level binding, so none is authorized and none is needed. This is acceptable precisely because Stella output is never authoritative (SB-03, SB-04): nothing that must be attributable to a decision depends on it.

controls.control: A Stella-drafted rationale is a UI PREFILL only. The persisted decision_rationale is what the designated human submitted at T5, attributed to decided_by. The system must not record a rationale the human did not submit, and must not mark a rationale as human-authored because it passed through a human's screen unedited without submission.

Stella availability is NOT a precondition for any Evaluate transition. Every transition T1..T8 must succeed with Stella unreachable, disabled, unconfigured or erroring. Evaluate degrades to fully functional without AI.

Evaluate must not extend canUseStella. The existing STELLA_ROLES set governs who may invoke Stella; Evaluate consumes it unchanged. Note that STELLA_ROLES includes reviewer and analyst — a role may be permitted to invoke Stella ANALYSIS while being excluded from deciding (HD-05) or from editing criterion responses (RAT-EV-02, reviewer). These are independent permissions and must not be cross-derived.

broad_evaluate.rule: Broad Evaluate Commercial V1 does NOT depend on Wave3 and does NOT depend on FIBIU-19 or FIBIU-20.
broad_evaluate.anchor: HD-15, verbatim: 'Evaluate V1 does NOT use first-class stella_findings and does NOT require an approved SROI run. Therefore broad Evaluate does not depend on Wave3.'
broad_evaluate.R1_position_superseded: R1's AG-05 held that RE_U3's EVALUATE_RUNTIME_STATUS = WAIT_FOR_WAVE3_CONTRACT 'stands until amended', while narrowing the question to an authority question rather than a data one. HD-15 is that amendment and answers the authority question. R1's analysis of the SHAPE was correct; the owner has now supplied the ANSWER. AG-05 is closed.
broad_evaluate.structural_confirmation: No object in OBJ-1..OBJ-4 carries a foreign key, a required read, or a transition guard against any FIBIU-19 or FIBIU-20 object. The independence is structural, not merely declared.

narrow_run_review.rule: The NARROW FIB run-review surface RETAINS its own independent Wave3 dependency, governed where FIB governs it. Evaluate does NOT absorb, replace, relocate, rename or re-implement it.
narrow_run_review.anchor: HD-15: 'A narrow run-review FIB surface may retain its independent Wave3 dependency.' HD-15's own implementation_status says it 'explicitly preserves rather than resolves' that carve-out.
narrow_run_review.what_is_preserved: lib/pipeline/methodology-review.ts, lib/pipeline/sroi-results.ts (assertRunMethodologyApprovalAllowed at line 317, called at 451 and 507), sroi_run_reviews, the review set via isInReviewSet, canApproveRunMethodology(role, isRunAuthor), and FIBDB-040's future sod_trigger — all remain owned by FIB / FIBIU-20.
narrow_run_review.relationship: RE_U3 calls methodology-review a CURRENT_IMPLEMENTATION_SUBSET of the future Evaluate area. That is an IA statement about product surface, NOT a licence to migrate the code. RE_U3's own prohibition_observed says it 'did not rename or relocate lib/pipeline/methodology-review.ts'. This package observes the same prohibition.
narrow_run_review.no_annexation: Evaluate must not annex stella_findings, stella_finding_dispositions, sroi_run_reviews or any FIBIU-20-owned object. Where an Evaluate criterion needs to reflect a run's methodology-review status it READS that status; it does not re-decide it, does not write to sroi_run_reviews, and does not reuse Evaluate's decision path to approve a run.

RLS_SECURITY_INVARIANTS.invariant: Every Evaluate relation has ROW LEVEL SECURITY ENABLED and FORCED.
RLS_SECURITY_INVARIANTS.precedent: db/migrations/0068_commercial_account_ce1.sql, which is ENABLE + FORCE with zero policies.

RLS_SECURITY_INVARIANTS.invariant: Every Evaluate relation carries a NOT NULL organization_id, denormalized where necessary, so no policy needs a join to be correct. The tenant predicate is exactly organization_id = ANY(current_user_org_ids()).
RLS_SECURITY_INVARIANTS.rationale: A policy that joins to reach organization_id is a policy whose correctness depends on the joined row's own policy. Also the enforcement of HD-10's organization-only template scope.

RLS_SECURITY_INVARIANTS.invariant: NO Evaluate policy contains current_user_is_super_admin(). Declared explicitly as the Evaluate instance of HD-12, because 15 migrations at BASE establish the opposite precedent and a new table written by imitation would inherit it.
RLS_SECURITY_INVARIANTS.verification: THREE-PART, and part 3 is new in R3. (1) A text assertion that the Evaluate migration contains zero occurrences of current_user_is_super_admin. (2) A real-PostgreSQL probe proving a super_admin principal with no membership reads zero rows from every Evaluate relation. (3) A CLOSED-WORLD assertion over ALL THREE policy lineages - db/migrations, db/prepared packet-only, and the hosted baseline - because the canonical census (docs/ops/security/PLATFORM_ADMIN_RLS_SUPERADMIN_POLICY_CENSUS_v1.0.0.json) measures 140 superadmin disjuncts distributed 127/9/4 across those three lineages and states verbatim that 'Closing db/migrations alone is insufficient and MUST NOT be reported as closure.' Evaluate is NOT responsible for closing the 140 pre-existing disjuncts, which the census assigns to the platform-admin successor. Stated so the widened verification is not misread as Evaluate inheriting a platform-wide remediation.

RLS_SECURITY_INVARIANTS.invariant: OBJ-2 has NO UPDATE policy and NO DELETE policy except the single write-once publication transition, plus the uellix_forbid_mutation trigger constrained to the same exception.

OBJ-3 UPDATE is permitted ONLY while state is pre-DECIDED and pre-ARCHIVED, and every snapshot column is write-once. A DECIDED row admits no UPDATE at all. DELETE is denied outright on OBJ-3 — a decided evaluation is audit-bearing.
OBJ-4 is INSERT-ONLY. There is NO UPDATE policy and NO DELETE policy on OBJ-4 at all, and INSERT is permitted only while the parent evaluation is pre-lock and not ARCHIVED.
RLS_SECURITY_INVARIANTS.rationale: This is what makes RAT-EV-03's traceability floor enforceable at the database rather than by convention: a response row that cannot be updated or deleted cannot lose its actor, role or timestamp. R1's upsert model would have required an UPDATE policy and would have made the floor unenforceable.
RLS_SECURITY_INVARIANTS.shape_conditionality: SHAPE-CONDITIONAL (BR NB-01). This is the correct enforcement FOR THE AUTHORIZED SHAPE in OBJ_4_SHAPE_CLASSIFICATION. An alternative conforming shape must supply its own equivalent database-level guarantee that a prior action's four traceability facts cannot be destroyed; it may not simply omit one. The INVARIANT is ratified; this particular policy shape is not.

RLS_SECURITY_INVARIANTS.invariant: The DECIDE write path additionally requires the actor's role, resolved via current_user_role_in_org(organization_id), to equal the row's designated_decision_role AND to be a member of the closed two-element decision set. Membership in the organization is necessary but NOT sufficient for T5.

The CRITERION-EDIT write path additionally requires the actor's role, resolved via current_user_role_in_org(organization_id), to be a member of the closed three-element edit set by exact identity, and requires recorded_by_role to EQUAL that resolved role — a client may not declare a role it does not hold.

created_by / recorded_by / decided_by / published_by / retired_by / archived_by must equal auth.uid() in the WITH CHECK of the writing policy, following the 0045 domain_object_versions_insert precedent (created_by = auth.uid()). A client-supplied actor id is never trusted.

Policies are granted TO uellix_app, not TO public, following the 0045 insert-policy precedent. A future ACL package must GRANT on the Evaluate tables to uellix_app or the runtime cannot read them — recorded because hosted_0007 already enumerates 37 tables and 15 FIB tables lack that grant.

Cross-organization reads are impossible by predicate, not by application filtering. A request whose principal resolves to no organization sees ZERO Evaluate rows — never all rows. Stated because a null/ambient scope has previously resolved to GLOBAL rather than to refusal elsewhere in this repository.
No Evaluate relation is exposed through any anonymous, public or unauthenticated surface (HD-14). There is no public locator, no share token and no verification endpoint for Evaluate in V1.

IMMUTABLE_SNAPSHOTS_AND_VERSIONING.write_once: No snapshot column may ever be updated after it is written. Enforced by the absence of an UPDATE policy for DECIDED rows (RLS-05) plus the immutability trigger.
IMMUTABLE_SNAPSHOTS_AND_VERSIONING.why_decided_by_role_is_snapshotted: A user's role in an organization can change after a decision. IMMUTABLE_SNAPSHOTS_AND_VERSIONING.why_score_is_snapshotted_and_also_deriva: The Score remains derivable from OBJ-4's current projection and the pinned OBJ-2, and it is ALSO snapshotted. That redundancy is deliberate and is a CONTROL: a mismatch between the snapshot and a fresh recomputation over unchanged inputs proves that something which was supposed to be immutable changed. See the test manifest M-05.
IMMUTABLE_SNAPSHOTS_AND_VERSIONING.two_version_lineages_and_why: Evaluate carries exactly TWO append-only lineages and no more: OBJ-2's template-version lineage, keyed (template_id, version) with a monotonic ordinal and supersedes_version_id; and OBJ-4's criterion-response lineage, keyed (evaluation_id, criterion_key, ordinal) with supersedes_response_id. R1 had only the first. The second is required by RAT-EV-03's traceability floor. DecisionPolicy has no lineage of its own (it rides OBJ-2's) and evaluations have none (they pin one OBJ-2 row for life).

That was a FALSE DICHOTOMY. HD-11 ratifies TWO route FAMILIES that both exist: one project-scoped and one organization-scoped. This package therefore does NOT invent specific URLs and does NOT keep an authority gap open merely because a pathname is an implementation decision.

prohibited_conflations: A REVIEW_REQUIREMENT is not an OWNER_AUTHORITY_GAP. Ten open reviews do not reopen a single decision.
An IMPLEMENTATION_DEPENDENCY is not an OWNER_AUTHORITY_GAP. The absent bounded support capability is a runtime fact, not an undecided question.

Closing an OWNER_AUTHORITY_GAP discharges nothing in any other dimension.

A BOUNDED_IMPLEMENTATION_CHOICE is not an OWNER_AUTHORITY_GAP and is not an IMPLEMENTATION_DEPENDENCY. It is a disclosed choice: the act exists, the authority had to bind it to be executable, and canonical text is silent on the act itself rather than silent inside a statement about it.

blockers.finding: The pristine R3 artifact violated its OWN predicate-identity contract. R3's PREDICATE_IDENTITY_SEPARATION.prohibitions stated 'No Evaluate predicate may be derived from another by reference to its role array; each names its own closed constant' - yet R3's own model had canArchiveEvaluation consuming EVALUATE_DECISION_ROLES, and its permission_matrix had canCreateEvaluation consuming EVALUATE_DECISION_ROLES as well.
blockers.verdict: CA WAS CORRECT, and the defect is of the exact class R3 itself identified. R3 wrote the rule, enumerated the extensional collisions that make the rule necessary, built N-22 to enforce it - and then two of its own six concepts shared a constant. Writing 'consumed, not redefined' next to a shared constant does not make the sharing conform; it documents the violation.
blockers.why_R3_missed_it: R3's validator checked that the six PREDICATES were distinct names and that the declared collision count matched the extensions. It never checked that the six CONSTANTS were distinct. The check was one field away from the defect.
blockers.closed_by: This revision. EVALUATE_ARCHIVE_ROLES and EVALUATE_CREATE_ROLES are introduced as distinct named constants, the model is extended to seven concepts, and the pairwise prohibition matrix is generated over all ordered pairs so it is complete by construction rather than by hand.
blockers.role_semantics_changed: NONE. Every admitted extension is byte-identical to R3. This repair is structural only.

why_this_does_NOT_convert_OWNER_AUTHORIT.taxonomy_test: This artifact's own definition of an OWNER_AUTHORITY_GAP is 'a product decision that no canonical ratification answers, where PROCEEDING WOULD REQUIRE THIS AUTHORITY TO INVENT THE ANSWER'. The operative clause is the second one.
why_this_does_NOT_convert_OWNER_AUTHORIT.asymmetry_with_BR_B-01: BR blocker B-01 was a blocker because HD-09 NAMED the act ('impact_manager may draft') and was silent only on whether organization_admin may also draft. There was a ratified statement whose scope R2 narrowed by encoding one reading. Here canonical text NAMES NO SUCH ACT at all, so there is no ratified statement being narrowed, widened or contradicted. This asymmetry is stated explicitly so an auditor can check the reasoning rather than accept the conclusion.
why_this_does_NOT_convert_OWNER_AUTHORIT.the_choice_widens_nothing: The chosen extension is a strict SUBSET of EVALUATE_CRITERION_EDIT_ROLES, is equal to the decision and archive extensions, and excludes all four roles HD-05 forbids from deciding plus super_admin. No role gains any capability it lacks elsewhere in the artifact, and no ratified exclusion is weakened.
why_this_does_NOT_convert_OWNER_AUTHORIT.the_act_is_preparatory_and_reversible: T1 produces a DRAFT evaluation: no Score snapshot, no recommended outcome, no decision, no immutable state, and it is archivable from DRAFT (T6). It confers no decision, publish or retire authority. Nothing irreversible or externally visible follows from creation alone.
why_this_does_NOT_convert_OWNER_AUTHORIT.conclusion: The create binding does NOT block this authority package. It is disclosed as an unresolved future authority surface rather than counted as an owner gap, and the implementing node is bound not to widen it.

CREATE_AUTHORITY_DISCLOSURE.obligation_on_the_implementing_node: Implement EVALUATE_CREATE_ROLES exactly as enumerated. Do NOT widen it, do NOT derive it from another constant, and do NOT treat its extensional equality with the decision or archive sets as licence to share a constant.
CREATE_AUTHORITY_DISCLOSURE.future_authority_path: If the owner wishes to ratify create-role authority, it is a one-clause amendment to the micro-ratifications ledger and would carry whatever review requirement the owner attaches. Until then this classification stands and is disclosed on every read of this artifact.
CREATE_AUTHORITY_DISCLOSURE.structural_benefit_of_separating_it_now: Because create now reads its own constant, a future amendment to HD-05 (decision) or HD-08 (archive) cannot silently move the create set - which is exactly the failure mode CA-B-01 left open.
